summary: Hood River County lookout cab built 1931 and removed 1955; a user report says only glass and metal remain, and the trail page lists the route closed.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Hood National Forest
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1955; a user report says only a few bits of glass and metal remain on the summit.

access.note: Forest Service page lists Tanner Butte Trail #401 as closed due to unstable conditions after the 2017 Eagle Creek Fire; restoration ongoing.

visit.trail_note: From the Wahclella Falls trailhead, a round trip of at least 18 miles, per the Oregon Hikers guide

notes_for_editor: Trail closure: the Forest Service trail page we read shows no date and says closed after the 2017 Eagle Creek Fire. The Oregon Hikers guide also labels the hike 'Closed' in its hike listing (text: 'Tanner Butte Difficult Closed'), so two sources report the closure; the story asks readers to check it before a trip. The statement about what remains rests on one undated SummitPost user report; no official source describes the summit today. The 1931 'new house' is presumed to be the L-4 cab, which the sources do not say outright. The 1931 Bull Run Reserve remark is left out. The record's kind 'ground' fits the L-4 cab; no correction proposed. The access level 'closed' describes the trail, not the site itself.
